{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Kubient)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of Exhibit 10.14 Master Services Agreement, dated 5 February
**Status of findings:** All findings below are drawn from the review record; verification was skipped on each item.

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against our contracting playbook. The commercial architecture is a non-exclusive revenue share, and several of the provisions we most often fight over — exclusivity, non-compete, minimum commitments, MFN, non-solicitation, customer-side audit rights and liquidated damages — are simply absent or already drafted in our favour. Those items need no redline, and we recommend actively preserving the non-exclusivity language in Section 1.

The risk in this deal is concentrated in three gaps rather than in aggressive vendor drafting. First, there is **no limitation of liability cap anywhere in the Agreement**; Section 7 excludes consequential damages only, leaving both parties exposed to unlimited direct liability. Second, there is **no intellectual property or data ownership article** — nothing confirms that we own our Content, Properties, Inventory, Requests or the visitor data Kubient collects and stores under Section 9(b)(iii), and nothing addresses deliverables. Third, our **indemnity in Section 10(b) is materially broader than Kubient's**, extending to breach of any representation or warranty plus an open-ended catch-all, while Kubient's Creative indemnity is diluted by a "best of its knowledge" qualifier for demand it controls.

Secondary but meaningful issues include a one-sided termination construct (no convenience right for us during the Initial Term, a 90-day exit notice on indefinite auto-renewal, and forfeiture of our revenue share during the notice period), a revocable licence that does not extend to our affiliates or contractors, the absence of transition assistance and data return on exit, no warranty remedy, and no vendor insurance covenant. Governing law is a one-word fix: Delaware law is paired with a New York forum, and we would align to New York law.

None of the findings is, on its face, a walk-away. The 90-day non-renewal notice sits at the walk-away boundary and the uncapped liability position should not be signed as drafted.

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section ref. | Issue in brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | Preamble | Our Section 10(b) indemnity is far broader than playbook (any rep/warranty breach plus open-ended catch-all); Kubient's Creative indemnity is cut back by a "best of its knowledge" qualifier. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | Preamble | No IP or data ownership article. Nothing confirms our ownership of Content, Properties, Inventory, Requests or visitor data, or of deliverables. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | Preamble | No monetary cap anywhere; Section 7 excludes consequential damages only. Unlimited direct liability for both parties. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | Preamble | Mutual clause with reasonableness standard and consent-free carve-outs for affiliates, asset sales and mergers. No change-of-control trigger. |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | Preamble | Section 1 expressly negates exclusivity; we remain free to use other agents or sell to third parties. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | Preamble | No LD, penalty or early-termination fee payable by us. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | Preamble | Grant runs to Customer only, is expressly revocable, non-transferable and non-assignable; no affiliate or contractor coverage. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | Preamble | No non-compete, field-of-use or territory restriction on our business. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | Preamble | No convenience right for us during the 12-month Initial Term; Kubient may exit for any reason on 90 days' notice and takes all fees generated during the notice period. |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Preamble | No audit, inspection or records-examination right exercisable against us. No redline (adding machinery would create a right that does not exist). |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | Preamble | Delaware law paired with an exclusive New York, New York forum; Section 8 AAA arbitration also conflicts with the exclusive court jurisdiction. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | Compliant | Preamble | No MFN or best-terms obligation in either direction. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | Preamble | Pure revenue share on actual activity; no minimum spend, take-or-pay or volume cap on us. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Compliant | Preamble | No non-solicit or no-hire covenant binding us. |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | Preamble | Indefinite 1-year auto-renewals with a 90-day exit notice; no renewal reminder and no cap on renewal pricing. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | Preamble | Section 4(c) covers only cessation, licence revocation and return of Confidential Information; no transition assistance, data export or deletion certification. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | Preamble | Warranty content is largely present and survives the Section 13 disclaimer, but there is no conformance-to-specification warranty and no warranty remedy anywhere. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | Preamble | No insurance clause at all, despite Kubient processing our visitor data under Section 9(b)(iii) and giving broad indemnities. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

On the findings before us, no provision constitutes an outright walk-away. Two items sit at or near the line and should be treated as non-negotiable in substance:

- **Uncapped liability (LOL-CAP, critical).** We should not sign with no cap in either direction. A fees-based cap alone would be illusory because Section 5 is a revenue share under which we pay Kubient no fees — hence the proposed formulation based on amounts paid or payable between the parties with a USD 1,000,000 floor.
- **90-day non-renewal notice (RENEWAL, medium).** The 90-day window on indefinite auto-renewal is three times our preferred position and beyond even the 60-day fallback, placing it at the walk-away boundary.

For completeness, the review confirms the absence of the classic walk-away triggers: no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right for Kubient, no foreign-seat arbitration (venue is court-based), no unlimited or unannounced audit rights and no remote access to our systems, and no assignment of our IP or data to Kubient.

---

## 4. Next steps

**Priority 1 — critical, must land before signature**

1. **Liability cap.** Add a mutual aggregate cap to Section 7 at the greater of 12 months' amounts paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement carved out as uncapped Excluded Claims.
2. **IP and data ownership.** Insert one ownership subsection: we own our Content, Properties and Customer Data; Kubient retains the Auction Platform and pre-existing tools; Kubient assigns deliverables with a perpetual royalty-free licence back to embedded Kubient IP; Kubient receives only a limited service-delivery licence in Customer Data; no joint ownership.
3. **Indemnities.** Narrow our Section 10(b) indemnity to the Content/Properties and our breach of applicable Law, and delete the "to the best of its knowledge" qualifier from Kubient's Creative indemnity — Kubient controls that demand and should stand behind it.

**Priority 2 — high**

4. **Licence scope.** Extend the grant to our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, limit revocation to expiration or termination under paragraph 4, and make the licence transferable on a permitted assignment under paragraph 14(h) so it tracks the assignment clause already agreed.
5. **Termination for convenience.** Add a 30-day convenience right for us with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, confine Kubient's convenience right to the end of the then-current term on 90 days' notice, and remove the fee forfeiture during the notice period. Fallback of 60 days' notice available.

**Priority 3 — medium and low**

6. **Renewal.** Keep the 12-month renewal term but cut the non-renewal/convenience notice to 30 days, add a Kubient renewal reminder 60 days out, and cap renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3%. Fallback: 60 days / 5%.
7. **Transition.** Insert a new Section 4(c)(v) requiring up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Customer Data in machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter. Fallback: 90 days' assistance with the same 30-day export.
8. **Warranty remedy.** Add a 90-day conformance-to-specification warranty with re-performance, repair/replacement or refund as new Section 9(b)(xii). Existing warranties already run for the Term.
9. **Governing law.** Change Delaware to New York to match the New York County forum, and flag Section 8's mandatory AAA arbitration for conforming against the exclusive court jurisdiction.
10. **Insurance.** Insert a vendor insurance covenant as new General Provisions subsection (j): CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, additional-insured status on CGL, certificates on request. Fallback: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.

**No action required:** ASSIGN, EXCLUSIVITY, LD, NONCOMPETE, AUDIT, MFN, MINCOMMIT, NOSOLICIT. We should preserve the Section 1 non-exclusivity language as drafted and re-check MFN and minimum-commitment exposure if and when commercial Exhibits are circulated, as those are not exposed in this document.

**Process note:** verification was skipped on all findings; we suggest a confirming pass against the executed exhibits before the redline goes out.
"}
